page: Amazon Web Services c7gn.large is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features an ARMv8 64-bit AWS Graviton processor utilizing the Neoverse-V1 microarchitecture clocked at 2.6 GHz. The instance configuration allocates 2 dedicated physical cores without hyperthreading, running 1 thread per core. Memory capacity is configured at 4.0 GB of RAM, establishing a 2.0 GB per-core compute-optimized memory ratio. The CPU topology incorporates 64 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache, alongside hardware AES cryptography extensions. This instance type contains no integrated GPUs and does not bundle local ephemeral storage, relying entirely on remote network-attached block volumes.

Benchmark results demonstrate consistent single-core efficiency paired with low aggregate multi-core throughput due to the 2-core footprint. Single-thread workloads perform solidly in the middle tier, evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 1514.0, a stress-ng single-core rating of 1532.89, and gzip compression throughput of 24.09 GB/sec. Large block read memory bandwidth reaches 57.94 GB/sec in the median band. Conversely, the low core count places multi-threaded operations in the lower quartile, yielding a Geekbench multi-core score of 2757.0, PassMark CPU score of 1580.01, and Redis performance of 3.43 million SET operations per second.

Networking performance is defined by a baseline bandwidth of 6 Gbps, which is substantial for a dual-core server profile. However, memory-intensive execution and write operations are constrained, reflecting a 20.86 GB/sec large-block memory write throughput and a low PassMark memory index of 1055.37. The total system allocation of 4.0 GB RAM precludes running larger container footprints or memory-resident databases.

The AWS c7gn.large provides an efficient, network-enhanced entry point for workloads requiring consistent single-thread execution alongside elevated network throughput. Typical fitting deployment scenarios include lightweight network appliances, API edge gateways, modest proxy routing, continuous integration worker agents, and entry-level arm64 compilation tasks that do not demand extensive local I/O or large working memory sets.
description: Amazon Web Services c7gn.large is a compute-optimized arm64 instance powered by a 2.6 GHz AWS Graviton Neoverse-V1 processor on the Nitro hypervisor. It provides 2 dedicated physical cores (1 thread per core) and 4.0 GB of RAM, offering a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio. The instance includes 32 MB of L3 cache, hardware AES acceleration, 6 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, zero bundled local storage, and no GPU hardware. Single-core performance falls in the median industry tier, producing a Geekbench single-core score of 1514.0 and gzip compression at 24.09 GB/sec, while multi-core compute and memory write speeds place in the lower quartiles due to the compact 2-core footprint. AWS c7gn.large is best suited for network-heavy lightweight applications, API gateways, proxy serving, and small-scale arm64 CI/CD microservices.
